newsitem.title: USA: Group urges NY to accept much of new welfare bill.
newsitem.headline: Group urges NY to accept much of new welfare bill.

text.p: New York state, grappling with the new federal welfare bill, was urged by a taxpayer's group on Tuesday to accept many of the bill's reforms even though New York City and a number of advocate groups say they are too harsh.

"The federal reforms give us an opportunity to overhaul New York's welfare programs to encourage work, strengthen families, and reduce fraud," Tom Carroll, president of CHANGE-NY, said in prepared remarks. The group calls itself the state's largest taxpayers association.

States can seek waivers from some of the strict federal rules, and Governor George Pataki has signaled he wants to opt out of restrictions on Medicaid benefits for legal immigrants. New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani has sued the federal government, challenging the constitutionality of new restrictions on welfare benefits for illegal aliens.

CHANGE-NY proposed stiffening some requirements on maternal and family leave. It said women on welfare should only get 12 weeks of leave after giving birth. The welfare reforms would exempt a mother with her first child from work for one year, but the 12-week rule would apply for any more children.
Some of the group's proposals were advanced by the Pataki Administration last spring. But the Republican governor's reforms were blocked by the state Assembly, which is controlled by Democrats.
